name: imadjust
expr: J = imadjust([0.0 0.5 1.0]); r1 = J(1); r2 = J(2); r3 = J(3); J1 = imadjust(I, [], []); e1 = double(isequal(J1, I)); J2 = imadjust(I, [], [0 1]); e2 = double(isequal(J2, I)); J3 = imadjust(I, [0 1], []); e3 = double(isequal(J3, I)); J4 = imadjust(I); ne4 = double(~isequal(J4, I)); j4 = double(J4(2,2)); J5 = imadjust(I, [0.2 0.8], [0 1], 2); j5 = double(J5(2,2));
comment: Sig: r = imadjust(...). DEEP-PROBE c169: an explicitly-passed empty [] for the in-range endpoints means MATLAB's default [0 1] (identity, NO stretch) — distinct from the ABSENT 1-arg form imadjust(I), which auto-stretches via stretchlim (1% saturation). numkit previously treated empty [] like the absent case (stretchlim), so imadjust(I,[],[]) wrongly contrast-stretched. Now e1=e2=e3=1 (empty in-range / empty out-range == identity), while ne4=1 and j4=204 confirm the 1-arg stretchlim form is preserved; j5 covers explicit-range + gamma=2 (j5=154). covers:[imadjust].
